entities.name: Adolphe Perraud
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adolphe Perraud (1828–1906) was a French cardinal and Oratorian priest who served as Bishop of Autun and became one of the most distinguished Catholic preachers and literary figures of late nineteenth-century France. Born in Lyon, he joined the Congregation of the Oratory and became renowned for his eloquence before being appointed Bishop of Autun in 1874 and elevated to cardinal in 1893.

Perraud's most notable achievement beyond his episcopal ministry was his election to the Académie française in 1882, making him one of a small number of Catholic prelates to sit among the Forty Immortals of French literature. His election was a cultural event in itself—a recognition that French Catholic intellectual life could produce figures of the highest literary distinction even in an era when the Third Republic was aggressively secularising French public life. He used his Académie platform to defend Catholic cultural contributions to French civilisation.

As Bishop of Autun, he administered a historically important diocese in Burgundy that had been a centre of French Christian culture since late antiquity. His theological and literary writings, combined with his Académie membership, made him the most publicly visible French Catholic intellectual of his generation. His career exemplifies the French Catholic attempt to maintain cultural prestige within a secularising republic by demonstrating the compatibility of faith and the highest standards of French intellectual life.
